title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 13

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the fault-category lesson begin?
tasks.audioText: The maintenance lecturer will compare common electrical fault descriptions on Monday at eleven thirty. Students should bring the fault-category worksheet. The lesson will distinguish open circuit, short circuit and intermittent fault as descriptive terms. Students will analyse written examples and identify what information is still needed before a cause can be confirmed.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which worksheet is required for the fault-category lesson?
tasks.audioText: The maintenance lecturer will compare common electrical fault descriptions on Monday at eleven thirty. Students should bring the fault-category worksheet. The lesson will distinguish open circuit, short circuit and intermittent fault as descriptive terms. Students will analyse written examples and identify what information is still needed before a cause can be confirmed.

tasks.prompt: An open circuit describes a break in a path where continuity is not present. A short circuit describes an unintended low-resistance connection between points. An intermittent fault occurs irregularly and may be difficult to reproduce. These terms describe different conditions, but a report should still record the evidence and test context rather than state a cause without confirmation. Reading 1. What does an open circuit describe?
options: A break in a path where continuity is not present

tasks.prompt: Why should a report include test context?
options: To record evidence and avoid an unsupported conclusion

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO fault categories and their descriptions.
options: Short circuit — a normal open connection
Open circuit — a type of sensor
Open circuit — a break in a path

tasks.prompt: A fault that occurs irregularly is described as ___.
A fault occurs only sometimes. Which description is most accurate?
options: The problem appears intermittently; further evidence is needed to identify the cause.
The fault is permanent because it happened once.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of electrical fault categories in a logical order.
options: Compare the observation with fault terminology
State what evidence is still needed
correctOrder: Compare the observation with fault terminology
State what evidence is still needed

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words comparing open-circuit, short-circuit and intermittent-fault descriptions. Explain why evidence is needed before identifying a cause.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: open-circuit, short-circuit and intermittent-fault descriptions are distinguished at a general level (0–2); the response explains why evidence is needed before identifying a cause (0–2); the explanation is clear with understandable grammar (0–2); fault/electrical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
